analysis.investment_thesis: Aavas Financiers is a high-quality affordable-housing lender with a seven-year net profit CAGR of 29.7% and a credible niche in semi-urban/rural markets where incumbent banks have little appetite. At forward P/E of 13.6x, the market is pricing in little growth — yet the business has compounded assets from ₹7,657 Cr to ₹18,618 Cr in five years with no visible credit crisis.
key_strengths: Net profit compounding at 29.7% CAGR over seven years — consistent execution is rare
24.7% FII ownership signals sophisticated institutional conviction in management quality
Proprietary in-house credit assessment for informal-income borrowers is a genuine, hard-to-replicate edge
key_risks: ROE of 13.9% is modestly below my 15% preferred floor; leverage (D/E 3.08x) is structurally needed to push it higher
Revenue was flat YoY (₹2,018 Cr in FY24 vs ₹1,988 Cr in FY25) — first growth stumble in seven years
Concentration in semi-urban Rajasthan/Gujarat geography; a regional economic shock has outsized impact
red_flags: Finance cost data shows ₹828 Cr in FY24 dropping to ₹5 Cr in FY25 — almost certainly a data reporting anomaly, warranting verification before full confidence in FY25 numbers
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Aavas serves the segment that large banks deliberately ignore — self-employed informal-income borrowers in Tier 3/4 towns. The in-house underwriting capability built over 14 years is not easily replicated by a new entrant; this is a narrow but real moat. The company has grown its loan book, net profit, and equity base without a significant NPA crisis even through COVID, which is powerful evidence of underwriting discipline.

The forward P/E of 13.6x is the most interesting number here: the market seems to be pricing near-zero growth following the FY25 revenue plateau. If the plateau is temporary (disbursement seasonality), this is a mild buying opportunity. If it signals a lending-cycle slowdown, the ROE could dip further. I would hold a position already owned and add selectively below P/B of 2x.
